newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat heads to Paris for talks on Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Arafat heads to Paris for talks on Mideast peace.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat flew to Paris on Monday for talks with French President Jacques Chirac and new Prime Minister Lionel Jospin in search of a way to break an impasse in the Middle East peace process.
"President Arafat has been invited at a short notice by President Chirac for important talks on the peace process," a senior PLO official said.

"The Europeans have asked France to play a leading role in breaking the impasse in the peace process and to co-ordinate with the United States to return to play a role in solving the crisis," said the official, who insisted on anonymity.

Arafat, president of the West Bank and Gaza areas transferred to Palestinian rule under a peace deal with Israel, was expected to arrive in the French capital around noon (1000 GMT), Palestinian officials in Paris said.
He was scheduled to have lunch with Chirac at the Elysee presidential palace before talks later in the afternoon with Jospin and Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine.
His meeting with France's new leftist prime minister was to be their first since Jospin took office earlier this month. A Jospin aide described the meeting as "a working visit" but gave no details.
An alliance of Socialists, Communists and Greens was swept into power in France in a June 1 parliamentary election, obliging the conservative Chirac to share power with Jospin's leftist government.
Chirac has tried hard in the past to involve France in the negotiations but Israel has resisted giving it a role as a peace broker, seeing Paris as biased in favour of the Arab states.
But Jospin has criticised France's previous rightist government, accusing it of paying too little attention to the views of Israel in formulating policy.
A role for Paris in the super-sensitive peace process would take on new dimensions in view of Chirac's sharing of power with Jospin.

Jospin and Chirac have vowed to speak with a single voice in managing French affairs, but after a month of power-sharing the first hints of differences between the president and the government have begun to surface.
Formal PLO-Israeli peace moves came to a halt in March after Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
A U.S. peace envoy failed in April to restart the talks.
Egypt stepped in and PLO officials said Cairo would continue to mediate between the sides despite its failure to persuade Israel to suspend settlement building for six months.
Israel has welcomed Egyptian mediation but it has traditionally resisted European involvement in its peace moves with the PLO.
